sections.label: Major Wars
sections.description: Full-scale conventional conflicts that shaped India's modern military identity.

operations.name: Indo-Pakistani War (1947–48)
operations.objective: Defend Jammu & Kashmir following its accession to India and repel the Pakistan-backed invasion.
operations.result: Indian strategic success followed by UN-mediated ceasefire — India retained Jammu, the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh.
operations.description: The first war between India and Pakistan began after Pakistan-backed tribal forces invaded Jammu and Kashmir. Following the Instrument of Accession, Indian forces were airlifted to Srinagar and successfully defended the Kashmir Valley, Jammu and Ladakh against the invasion.
operations.significance: Established India's military defence of Jammu and Kashmir and secured the Jammu region, Kashmir Valley and Ladakh under Indian administration.

operations.name: Sino-Indian War (1962)
operations.location: Ladakh and North-East Frontier Agency (present-day Arunachal Pradesh)
operations.objective: Defend India's northern borders against Chinese military offensives and preserve India's territorial position.
operations.result: Indian military defeat — China retained Aksai Chin after declaring a unilateral ceasefire.
operations.description: China launched coordinated attacks across the western and eastern sectors of the disputed border. Indian forces fought under severe logistical and preparedness disadvantages; China declared a unilateral ceasefire and withdrew in the eastern sector while retaining control over Aksai Chin.
operations.significance: The defeat exposed major shortcomings in India's preparedness and led to extensive expansion, modernization, infrastructure development and doctrinal reform of the Indian Armed Forces.

operations.name: Indo-Pakistani War (1965)
operations.objective: Repel Pakistani aggression launched through Operation Gibraltar and defend Indian territory.
operations.result: Indian strategic success followed by UN-mediated ceasefire; Pakistan failed to achieve its principal objectives and no lasting territorial changes resulted.
operations.description: The conflict followed Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar infiltration into Jammu & Kashmir. India responded by opening multiple fronts across the international border, including operations towards Lahore, and successfully checked Pakistani offensives in major battles such as Asal Uttar.
operations.significance: Demonstrated India's ability to counter large-scale Pakistani conventional attacks and prevented Pakistan from achieving its principal military objectives.

operations.name: Indo-Pakistani War (1971)
operations.objective: Defend India against Pakistani attacks and support the liberation of Bangladesh.
operations.result: Decisive Indian Victory — surrender of approximately 93,000 Pakistani personnel and creation of Bangladesh.
operations.description: The war began after Pakistan launched pre-emptive air strikes on Indian airfields. The Indian Armed Forces conducted coordinated operations on the Eastern and Western Fronts, leading to the fall of Dhaka and the surrender of approximately 93,000 Pakistani personnel on 16 December 1971.
operations.significance: One of India's greatest military victories, resulting in the creation of Bangladesh and a major strategic and geopolitical transformation of South Asia.

operations.name: Kargil War (1999)
operations.location: Kargil, Dras, Batalik and Mushkoh sectors, Ladakh
operations.objective: Evict Pakistani forces and intruders occupying strategic heights on the Indian side of the Line of Control.
operations.result: Indian Victory — all major occupied positions regained.
operations.description: After Pakistani forces occupied strategic heights on the Indian side of the Line of Control, India launched coordinated military operations — Operation Vijay on land and Operation Safed Sagar from the air — to recapture the positions. 26 July is observed as Kargil Vijay Diwas.
operations.significance: Reaffirmed India's control over its territory and the sanctity of the Line of Control, while demonstrating India's capability to conduct high-altitude warfare under extreme conditions.

sections.label: Military Operations
sections.description: Named operations spanning integration of territories, overseas deployments, and precision strikes.

operations.name: Operation Polo
operations.objective: Integrate the princely State of Hyderabad into the Indian Union.
operations.result: Indian Victory — Hyderabad State Forces surrendered within five days.
operations.description: Officially termed a 'Police Action', Operation Polo resulted in the rapid surrender of the Nizam's forces and brought Hyderabad into the Indian Union.
operations.significance: Completed the political and territorial integration of one of India's largest and most strategically located princely states.

operations.name: Operation Bison
operations.location: Zoji La, Dras and Kargil, Ladakh
operations.objective: Recapture Zoji La Pass and reopen the land route to Ladakh.
operations.result: Indian Victory — Zoji La and Dras recaptured and the advance towards Kargil secured.
operations.description: Indian forces launched a surprise armoured assault through Zoji La using M5 Stuart tanks, recapturing the pass and Dras before advancing towards Kargil and restoring the route to Ladakh.
operations.significance: Marked one of the earliest major uses of tanks at extreme altitude in combat and played a crucial role in securing Ladakh for India during the 1947–48 war.

operations.name: Operation Vijay (Goa)
operations.objective: Liberate Goa, Daman and Diu from Portuguese colonial rule and integrate them into India.
operations.result: Indian Victory — Portuguese forces surrendered within approximately 36 hours.
operations.description: The Indian Armed Forces launched a coordinated land, air and naval campaign that resulted in the surrender of Portuguese forces and ended more than four centuries of Portuguese colonial rule in Goa, Daman and Diu.
operations.significance: Completed the territorial integration of Goa, Daman and Diu into India and ended Portuguese colonial rule on the Indian subcontinent.

operations.name: Operation Meghdoot
operations.objective: Secure the Saltoro Ridge and Siachen Glacier before Pakistan could occupy the area.
operations.result: Indian Victory — dominant heights secured and Indian control established.
operations.description: A pre-emptive operation launched by the Indian Army and Indian Air Force to occupy strategically important heights on the Saltoro Ridge and Siachen Glacier. India secured the dominant positions and has maintained control over the key heights.
operations.significance: Established Indian control over the Siachen Glacier and denied Pakistan control of the strategically vital Saltoro Ridge.

operations.name: Operation Falcon
operations.objective: Counter Chinese military presence in the Sumdorong Chu Valley and secure Indian positions.
operations.result: Indian strategic success — Chinese advance contained and escalation prevented.
operations.description: The Indian Army rapidly deployed troops to dominate the surrounding heights after Chinese troops moved into the Sumdorong Chu area, preventing further Chinese consolidation and strengthening India's position in the eastern sector.
operations.significance: Marked India's firm military response to Chinese border assertiveness and significantly improved India's defensive posture along the eastern LAC.

operations.name: Operation Rajiv
operations.objective: Capture Pakistan's heavily fortified Quaid Post overlooking Indian positions.
operations.result: Indian Victory — Quaid Post captured and renamed Bana Top.
operations.description: Indian troops successfully assaulted and captured the strategically important Quaid Post after intense fighting at extreme altitude. The position was renamed Bana Top in honour of Naib Subedar Bana Singh, who was awarded the Param Vir Chakra.
operations.significance: One of the most daring Indian high-altitude assaults, securing India's tactical advantage in the Bilafond La sector.

operations.name: Operation Pawan
operations.objective: Disarm the LTTE and implement the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord as part of the IPKF mission.
operations.result: Mission completed — IPKF withdrew March 1990.
operations.description: Indian forces conducted large-scale combat operations against the LTTE after the peace process collapsed, carrying out conventional and counter-insurgency operations across northern Sri Lanka, including the Battle of Jaffna.
operations.significance: One of the Indian Army's largest overseas military operations and a defining experience in urban, jungle and counter-insurgency warfare.

operations.name: Operation Cactus
operations.objective: Restore the legitimate government of the Maldives following an attempted coup.
operations.result: Indian Victory — legitimate government restored within hours.
operations.description: The Indian Armed Forces rapidly deployed paratroopers and a naval task force to Malé after a mercenary-backed coup attempt, securing the capital and restoring the legitimate government in under 24 hours.
operations.significance: Demonstrated India's rapid power-projection capability and reinforced its role as a major security provider in the Indian Ocean Region.

operations.name: Operation Parakram
operations.location: India–Pakistan International Border and Line of Control
operations.objective: Mobilize military pressure and compel Pakistan to act against cross-border terrorism following the Parliament attack.
operations.result: Strategic deterrence achieved — sustained military pressure without full-scale war.
operations.description: India carried out one of its largest military mobilizations after the terrorist attack on the Indian Parliament. Major Army strike formations were deployed along the western frontier, creating sustained conventional pressure on Pakistan.
operations.significance: Demonstrated India's ability to rapidly mobilize large conventional forces and shaped subsequent Indian thinking on rapid conventional response to terrorism.

operations.name: Operation Vijay
operations.objective: Recapture Indian territory occupied by Pakistani forces during the Kargil conflict.
operations.result: Indian Victory — all major occupied positions recaptured.
operations.description: Operation Vijay was the Indian Army's campaign during the Kargil War. Through sustained infantry assaults on near-vertical cliffs supported by artillery and air power, Indian forces regained major occupied positions including Tololing, Tiger Hill and Point 4875.
operations.significance: Demonstrated exceptional courage and endurance by Indian troops at extreme altitude and validated the importance of combined-arms warfare.

operations.name: Operation Safed Sagar
operations.objective: Provide air support to Indian Army ground operations during the Kargil War.
operations.result: Indian Victory — Indian air support successfully contributed to the recapture of occupied positions.
operations.description: The Indian Air Force launched Operation Safed Sagar to support ground operations by striking Pakistani positions, supply routes and logistics under strict rules of engagement that prohibited crossing the Line of Control.
operations.significance: Marked the first large-scale combat use of air power by the IAF since 1971 and highlighted the importance of joint Army–Air Force operations.

operations.name: Operation Ginger
operations.objective: Conduct a retaliatory cross-LoC raid following attacks on Indian soldiers.
operations.result: Indian operation completed — Pakistani military positions targeted.
operations.description: Indian Army personnel carried out a covert cross-Line of Control raid targeting Pakistani military positions in retaliation for attacks on Indian troops along the LoC.
operations.significance: An early known modern cross-LoC retaliatory operation that preceded the publicly acknowledged precision strikes of 2016.

operations.name: Operation Hot Pursuit
operations.objective: Neutralize militant camps responsible for the Manipur ambush on an Indian Army convoy.
operations.result: Indian Victory — militant camps targeted and significant casualties inflicted.
operations.description: Following an ambush on an Indian Army convoy in Manipur that killed 18 soldiers, Indian Special Forces conducted a cross-border operation against insurgent camps along the India–Myanmar border.
operations.significance: Demonstrated India's willingness to conduct precise cross-border counter-insurgency operations against groups responsible for attacks on Indian forces.

operations.name: 2016 Surgical Strikes
operations.location: Line of Control, Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir
operations.objective: Destroy terrorist launch pads used for infiltration following the Uri attack.
operations.result: Indian Victory — multiple terrorist launch pads destroyed.
operations.description: The Indian Army conducted precision cross-Line of Control strikes on multiple terrorist launch pads in Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir following the Uri terrorist attack that killed 19 Indian soldiers.
operations.significance: Marked a major shift toward publicly acknowledged precision cross-border retaliation against terrorist infrastructure.

operations.name: Operation Snow Leopard
operations.objective: Secure dominating heights along the LAC and strengthen India's defensive posture during the 2020 standoff.
operations.result: Indian strategic success — Kailash Range heights secured and India's tactical position strengthened.
operations.description: Indian Army formations including the Special Frontier Force occupied key heights on the Kailash Range south of Pangong Tso, gaining significant tactical advantage during the Eastern Ladakh standoff.
operations.significance: Strengthened India's negotiating position during subsequent military and diplomatic talks with China and demonstrated India's ability to rapidly occupy tactically dominant ground.

operations.name: Operation Sindoor
operations.objective: Destroy terrorist infrastructure linked to the Pahalgam terror attack.
operations.result: Indian operation completed — multiple terrorist infrastructure sites struck.
operations.description: India launched precision strikes against multiple terrorist infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack, using missiles and loitering munitions before a period of military escalation and subsequent ceasefire understanding.
operations.significance: Marked a major Indian precision cross-border operation against terrorist infrastructure and demonstrated integrated tri-service military capabilities.

sections.label: Internal Security Operations
sections.description: Operations to restore law and order within India's borders.

operations.name: Operation Blue Star
operations.objective: Remove heavily armed militants from the Golden Temple complex and restore law and order.
operations.result: Military objective achieved — militants removed from the complex.
operations.description: The Indian Army conducted Operation Blue Star to remove heavily armed militants who had fortified themselves inside the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar following months of escalating violence and militancy in Punjab.
operations.significance: One of the most consequential and controversial internal security operations in independent India's history, with major political, military and social consequences.

sections.label: Counter-Insurgency Operations
sections.description: Long-running campaigns against insurgent groups in India's northeast and Jammu & Kashmir.

operations.name: Operation Rakshak
operations.objective: Counter insurgency, eliminate militant networks and maintain internal security in Jammu & Kashmir.
operations.result: Ongoing — Indian security forces continue counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations.
operations.description: Operation Rakshak is the Indian Army's long-running counter-insurgency campaign in Jammu & Kashmir, conducted alongside other security forces to combat terrorism, cross-border infiltration and militant networks.
operations.significance: Represents one of the longest continuous counter-insurgency commitments undertaken by the Indian Army, spanning more than three decades.

operations.name: Operation Bajrang
operations.objective: Neutralize ULFA insurgents and dismantle militant infrastructure across Assam.
operations.result: Partial success — ULFA infrastructure and freedom of movement significantly disrupted.
operations.description: The first large-scale counter-insurgency operation against ULFA involved coordinated military sweeps of militant camps, weapons caches and leadership hideouts across Upper Assam.
operations.significance: Marked the beginning of sustained Indian Army operations against ULFA and established methods for subsequent counter-insurgency campaigns in Assam.

operations.name: Operation Rhino
operations.objective: Continue counter-insurgency operations against ULFA and restore normalcy in Assam.
operations.result: Ongoing — ULFA significantly weakened.
operations.description: Launched after Operation Bajrang, Operation Rhino combined military operations with intelligence-based actions to dismantle ULFA's operational capabilities and infrastructure across Assam.
operations.significance: Became one of the Indian Army's longest-running counter-insurgency operations in Northeast India.

operations.name: Operation Sarp Vinash
operations.location: Hilkaka Forest, Poonch District, Jammu & Kashmir
operations.objective: Destroy militant bases and eliminate terrorist infiltration routes in the Hilkaka region.
operations.result: Indian Victory — major militant stronghold dismantled.
operations.description: A month-long cordon-and-search operation conducted in the dense forests of Poonch that dismantled a major militant stronghold in Jammu & Kashmir and disrupted infiltration and terrorist infrastructure.
operations.significance: Significantly weakened terrorist infrastructure in the Pir Panjal region and disrupted infiltration routes used by Pakistan-backed militants.

operations.name: Operation All Out
operations.objective: Neutralize active terrorist networks through coordinated intelligence-based operations.
operations.result: Ongoing — significant terrorist leadership and networks eliminated.
operations.description: A coordinated counter-terrorism campaign involving the Indian Army, Jammu & Kashmir Police and Central Armed Police Forces to eliminate terrorist leadership and infrastructure through intelligence-driven targeted operations.
operations.significance: Marked a decisive shift towards intelligence-driven joint-force counter-terrorism in Jammu & Kashmir and significantly reduced active militant strength.

sections.label: Border Conflicts & Standoffs
sections.description: Military confrontations and standoffs along India's disputed borders.

operations.name: Operation Brasstacks
operations.objective: Conduct large-scale mechanised warfare exercises to validate operational doctrines.
operations.result: Exercise completed — demonstrated India's large-scale conventional capability and triggered a serious military crisis with Pakistan.
operations.description: One of the largest military exercises conducted by the Indian Army, involving large-scale troop and armour mobilisation in Rajasthan. Pakistan's counter-mobilisation brought the two countries close to armed confrontation.
operations.significance: Demonstrated India's large-scale conventional warfare capability and had major implications for Indian and Pakistani military planning.

operations.name: Eastern Ladakh Standoff
operations.objective: Maintain the status quo and defend India's territorial interests along the Line of Actual Control.
operations.result: Ongoing — Indian forces maintained a strong defensive posture and partial disengagement achieved at several friction points.
operations.description: A prolonged military standoff between Indian and Chinese forces across multiple friction points in Eastern Ladakh involving large-scale troop deployments, military infrastructure and successive rounds of military and diplomatic negotiations.
operations.significance: Represents one of the largest military deployments along the India–China border in decades and fundamentally reshaped India's border posture, infrastructure and modernization priorities.

operations.name: Galwan Valley Clash
operations.objective: Defend Indian positions and enforce disengagement agreements along the Line of Actual Control.
operations.result: Indian positions held — casualties on both sides.
operations.description: Indian and Chinese troops engaged in violent hand-to-hand combat in the Galwan Valley, resulting in the deaths of 20 Indian soldiers, including Colonel Santosh Babu. India retained its positions while Chinese casualties were also suffered.
operations.significance: Fundamentally altered India's military and diplomatic posture along the LAC and accelerated defence modernization, infrastructure development and forward deployment.

operations.name: Yangtse Clash
operations.objective: Prevent Chinese troops from altering the status quo along the Line of Actual Control.
operations.result: Indian positions held — Chinese attempt repelled.
operations.description: Chinese troops attempted to alter the status quo at Yangtse in the Tawang sector. Indian troops successfully resisted the attempt in a face-off involving hand-to-hand contact, with casualties and injuries reported on both sides.
operations.significance: Reaffirmed India's resolve and capability to defend the eastern sector of the LAC and prompted continued strengthening of India's Arunachal Pradesh border posture.
